title: Find the First Suspicious Transaction Value
real_world_story: A financial monitoring system maintains transaction amounts in sorted order. A transaction amount equal to or greater than a configured suspicious threshold needs to be identified quickly.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Binary Search for finding the first transaction amount that reaches or exceeds the threshold

problem_statement: Given a sorted array of transaction amounts and a threshold value T, find the index of the first transaction amount that is greater than or equal to T. If no such transaction exists, print -1.
task: Use Binary Search to locate the first transaction amount that meets or exceeds the suspicious threshold.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N. The second line contains N space-separated transaction amounts in non-decreasing order. The third line contains the threshold T.
output_format: Print the zero-based index of the first transaction amount greater than or equal to T. If no transaction meets the threshold, print -1.
constraints: Transaction amounts are sorted in non-decreasing order

examples.explanation: The first transaction amount greater than or equal to 400 is 450 at index 4.
No transaction amount reaches the threshold of 300.

expected_algorithm.name: Binary Search
expected_algorithm.reason: Because the transaction amounts are sorted, Binary Search can locate the first value meeting the threshold in logarithmic time.

hint: If the middle value is at least the threshold, store it as a possible answer and search the left half.
The final stored position is the first qualifying transaction.
real_world_takeaway: Binary Search allows financial monitoring systems to quickly locate threshold-crossing transactions when transaction data is maintained in sorted order.
